resources.string: Everheard turns the conversations you are part of into text, commitments, and a project timeline. It does not keep the audio.
A persistent notification and a start tone. There is no covert mode.
Audio is deleted after transcription. The database is encrypted with a key in Android Keystore.
Capture is armed all day, but paused 23:30–07:00 by default. You can edit the schedule later.
I understand that I may only record conversations I am legally allowed to record.
You can change all of this later in Settings.

In one-party-consent places you may record conversations you are part of. Recording bystanders who are not part of your conversation is not covered, and some places require everyone to agree. Everheard shows a notification and plays a tone while capturing. You are responsible for consent.
Everheard needs the microphone to turn speech into text. Capture stays visible in the notification shade.
Android requires a notification for a foreground recording service. It is also how the people around you can see that capture is on.
The setup is complete. Capture, transcription, and the timeline are being built in the next milestones.
A foreground service that stays armed, gates the microphone by schedule, and releases it during sleep. It lands in M0-T3.
